source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Flat supine with the head fixed straight, because this reliably prevents secretions or vomit from entering the airway in an unresponsive person.","B":"High-Fowler position without support, because an unresponsive client can reliably maintain trunk and airway alignment while seated upright.","C":"Prone face-down with the airway covered, because this position is recommended to prevent aspiration in all unconscious clients.","D":"A side-lying recovery position that maintains airway patency and permits fluid to drain, while continuing to monitor breathing."}}
source_row.rationale: For an unresponsive person breathing normally without a contraindication to movement, the recovery position is side-lying to help maintain airway patency and drainage while breathing is monitored.
source_row.source_detail: Recovery position recommendation: place an unresponsive person who is breathing normally and does not require CPR in a side-lying recovery position when no condition requires keeping them supine. 2024 American Heart Association/American Red Cross First Aid Guidelines; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: AHA/American Red Cross — 2024 First Aid Guidelines
source_row.stem: An unresponsive client is breathing normally and has no suspected spine or major trauma. Which position helps maintain an open airway while awaiting further care?
